title: voyage-batch checkpoint callback injects feedback for mesh-probe failures
description: During an interactive claude-harness-test session, the DSL validated syntactically but the mesh probe failed ('Non-manifold or duplicate face edge'). The round_callback in voyage/batch.py only injects visual feedback when the render base64 is present, which requires _render_dsl_headless to succeed, which requires the mesh probe to succeed. Net effect: when the agent writes a DSL that parses fine but produces non-manifold topology, the agent sees NOTHING — no error, no feedback — and is left waiting for the next round with no clue what went wrong. The agent only discovers the issue by calling validate_dsl explicitly. Fix: when validate_and_export_dsl returns a result with meshProbe.ok=false or no base64, inject a user message containing the mesh-probe error text so the agent can iterate.
definition-of-done: 1. voyage/batch.py _visual_round_callback handles the 'valid DSL but broken mesh' case by appending a user message with the mesh probe error. 2. Agent receives the error on its next round instead of silent success. 3. Claude-harness-test reproduction: write a DSL that triggers non-manifold output; verify the error is surfaced in the next round's request.json messages list.
testing-plan: 1. Write a minimal DSL that mirrors a cube onto itself (non-manifold trigger). 2. Run via claude-harness-test interactive mode. 3. Confirm the next round's last user message carries the non-manifold error text.
